metadata.method_name: r_prior causal test: language-conditioned refusal prior as the carrier of English abliteration's Slovene residual

frozen_predictions.outcome_set: OUTCOME = S3 JBB half B (41 harmful/benign twin pairs) + S4 StrongREJECT 'hoc' held-out categories (70 pairs); 111 harmful + 111 harmless items per language (EN, SL). residual := judged SL harmful refusal rate under A1 (d_EN).
frozen_predictions.primary_label_source: openai/gpt-4.1 blind judge (frozen rubric); if unavailable, the narrow opener rule labeller (flagged)
frozen_predictions.F1: rate_SL(d_EN) - rate_SL(d_EN+r_prior) >= 0.5 * rate_SL(d_EN) AND one-sided 95% item-cluster bootstrap LB of [cut(r_prior) - max_k cut(rand_k)] > 0. F1-hoc: same point estimate >= 0.5*residual on the 70 hoc items alone.
frozen_predictions.F2: under d_EN+r_prior: SL FLORES dev-B NLL change <= 0.1 nat/token AND (malformed + wrong-language + empty) rate on SL outputs <= 5%.
frozen_predictions.F3: r_prior alone (A3): judged SL harmless over-refusal falls by >= 50% relative vs no-op AND |EN harmful refusal change| < 0.10.
frozen_predictions.F4: d_EN+l (A4) and d_EN+u_SL (A5) each achieve < 0.5 x the F1 cut(r_prior).
frozen_predictions.F5: community model: r_prior weight edit lowers judged SL harmful refusal on hoc by >= 0.30 at <= 0.1 nat FLORES cost; EVALUABLE only if community SL hoc refusal >= 0.40.
frozen_predictions.F6: (exploratory) ADDING r_prior at L_r (alpha frozen) raises judged EN harmless refusal by >= 0.20 absolute over no-op.

KILL.a: cut(r_prior) not above best matched random (LB <= 0)
KILL.c: d_EN+r_prior_shuf (A10) achieves >= 50% of the r_prior cut

CONFOUND_RULES.language_identity: if A6 (r_prior perp l) fails F1 while A4 (d_EN+l) passes -> the effect is the language-identity component, not a refusal prior
CONFOUND_RULES.one_knob: if r_prior alone (A3) drops EN harmful refusal >= 0.10 -> 'one-knob' reading (2602.02132)

frozen_predictions.multiplicity: Holm across {F1 contrast vs best random, F3 over-refusal drop, F4 (two contrasts), F5}
frozen_predictions.statistics: item-cluster bootstrap over semantic ids (2000 reps; EN/SL and harmful/harmless twins resampled together); paired McNemar exact tests

fetched abstracts 2026-09-23: 2603.27518, 2609.16204, 2505.17306 (PolyRefuse, 14 languages; abstract reports near-perfect EN->X transfer, Slovene not named)

closest_sources.what_they_do: false-refusal vector = mean(pseudo-harmful) - mean(harmless), partially orthogonalized against the true refusal vector, ablated at all layers/positions; English only
closest_sources.delta: operator is identical (r_prior is a Wang-style false-refusal vector); new here: the refused-vs-complied contrast is built on judged HARMLESS refusals that are ~80% Slovene, it is tested as the carrier of English abliteration's residual refusal in another language, at matched EN efficacy, against language-identity / shuffled-label / collateral-matched random controls, and on a held-out community Heretic edit

closest_sources.what_they_do: adds an English-derived refusal vector at one layer and ablates an orthogonalized false-refusal vector at all layers to transfer English SAFETY to 8 languages (increase refusal, limit over-refusal)
closest_sources.delta: opposite goal and direction of effect (they add refusal cross-lingually; we ask whether a language-conditioned prior explains refusal that English REMOVAL leaves behind); no language-identity control or held-out edit reported in the abstract

closest_sources.id: arXiv:2505.17306 (Refusal direction is universal across safety-aligned languages; NeurIPS 2025)
closest_sources.what_they_do: English-derived refusal direction bypasses refusal in other languages near-perfectly
closest_sources.delta: iteration-1 A1 found the opposite in Gemma-3-12B for Slovene (85% residual SL refusal after d_EN ablation, cos 0.92); this artifact tests what carries that residual

closest_sources.id: arXiv:2602.02132 (There is more to refusal than a single direction)
closest_sources.what_they_do: geometrically distinct refusal-category directions give near-identical refusal/over-refusal trade-offs (one-knob)
closest_sources.delta: pre-registered rival: F3 requires language specificity (|EN harmful change| < 0.10)

closest_sources.id: arXiv:2608.08032 (Decided Upstream, Written Late; Kompella & Mahajan, Aug 2026)
closest_sources.what_they_do: Indic MoE (Sarvam): harm detection is language-invariant (cos ~0.9) but the refusal WRITER is language-dependent and late; head-level interventions
closest_sources.delta: closest conceptual neighbour (language-dependent refusal writing despite shared harm direction); different model family, circuit-level not direction-level, no abliteration residual or matched-random test

closest_sources.id: arXiv:2603.27518 (Maskey, Dras, Naseem; Over-Refusal and Representation Subspaces, Mar/Sep 2026)
closest_sources.what_they_do: probing shows harmful-refusal directions are task-agnostic while over-refusal directions are task-dependent (live inside benign task clusters); argues global over-refusal ablation fails; English only
closest_sources.delta: a mechanistic prior for why a POOLED, language-conditioned r_prior may be dominated by the refused items' composition (here: language) rather than by a transferable refusal prior; we test the multilingual, causal, post-abliteration version

closest_sources.id: arXiv:2609.16204 (Muhamed, Diab, Smith; Decoy Direction Optimization, Sep 2026)
closest_sources.what_they_do: post-hoc defence that makes abliteration ablate a decoy direction while safety stays intact; no multilingual component
closest_sources.delta: not a scoop; relevant as a reminder that a residual after abliteration can reflect where safety actually lives rather than a missing extra direction

novelty.verdict: not scooped on (i) language-conditioned prior as the carrier of English-abliteration residual and (ii) matched-efficacy stacking on an optimizer-selected edit; the operator itself is prior art (Wang et al. 2025) and the 'shared detection / language-dependent writing' framing is anticipated by 2608.08032 for a different model family - cite both.

deviations.deviation: Layer selection, matched efficacy, shuffle-median choice and weight-band choice use R1 (first-token log-odds) instead of R_seq

deviations.deviation: Batching certification gate: 13/16 prompts identical over 32 tokens (< 15/16); batched left-padded generation accepted by amendment because all 16 refusal classes matched and every divergence was late bf16 drift (no corruption)

deviations.deviation: Layer-selection filter relaxed: no candidate layer passed Dolly first-token KL < 0.1 (KL 0.41-12 at all 20 layers); the plan fallback (smallest FLORES among top-3 drops) would have chosen h=12 with FLORES +7.4 nats. deviations.reason: decided on HALF_A only, before freeze; KL failure is itself a finding (r_prior ablation shifts first-token distributions on harmless Dolly prompts)
